note: Missouri River boat-ramp access at the town of Miami, just west of the Highway 41 bridge, with a privy. MDC's primitive camping spot is on the gravel spur that runs west from the ramp lot along the riverbank, behind a thin line of trees. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: map-designated primitive camping on a gravel spur west of the ramp lot (GIS 450 = the pin, 67 m W of lot 880), not the ramp lot itself. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Pin fine; phone matches; riverview kept.
flags: INCLUSION OK: area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Designated Camping Sites'; 'There is a concrete boat ramp to access the Missouri River and a privy located on the area.' The area map (© 3/09) draws a gravel road running west from the parking lot to a turnaround, with the 'Primitive Camping Area' symbol beside it, apart from the lot/ramp/privy cluster; GIS 27 point 450 'Primitive Camping Area'. A designated point, so the ramp-lot drop rule does not apply. Rule 140 standard; no special-use-only rule, no Rule 101.

PIN fine: stored 39.32554,-93.22921 = GIS 450, on the gravel spur ~67 m W of the ramp lot (GIS 26 lot 880, 39.32569,-93.22844). The spur is wide graded gravel on imagery, reached from Main Street through the town of Miami on paved/gravel streets; a 23-ft rig reaches it. No ford or posted limit.

WATERFRONT: riverview kept. The spur is ~25-30 m from the Missouri River (~300 m wide) across a riprap bank with a single thin line of trees (leaf-off imagery shows open water through it); the page captions a photo 'View across the Missouri River at the Miami Access'. Trees on the bank block an open apron, so not riverfront.
HORSES: none. CLUSTERS: one camping point.
